question: Can ordinary paired sample covariance be reused as a cross-technique covariance objective when one endpoint is a Markov-chain estimator?
hypothesis: The ordinary sample-level covariance contract is insufficient because chain autocorrelation and chain-owned normalization require independent replicate-level evidence.

inputs.source_identity: HT.2 paired pilot covariance, HT.3 scheduler and HT.4 joint-sample contract

reproducibility.seed_policy: No stochastic conclusion is inferred; deterministic contract validation rejects the malformed evidence class.
reproducibility.determinism: The Technique Graph correlation model and covariance-edge identities fully determine the rejection.

baseline: Keep independent estimators and normalized MCMC chain replicates as separate aggregation strata until valid replicate covariance exists.
candidate: Insert sample-level cross covariance between an independent estimator and PSSMLT into the HT.3 objective.

result.conclusion: The proposed shortcut is rejected. A future multiplexed MCMC experiment must provide independent chain replicate namespaces, chain normalization and a covariance statistic defined over normalized replicates.

known_failure_domain: The rejection does not prove that correlation-aware aggregation with MCMC is impossible.
A future replicated-chain covariance contract may make the combination admissible.
This capsule closes only the ordinary sample-covariance shortcut.
